fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Paul says, "…I bow my knees before the Father…" (Ephesians 3:14), and he calls himself "an ambassador in chains" (Ephesians 6:20) and "the prisoner of Christ Jesus" (Ephesians 3:1). Whatever his chains were doing, his knees were still free to bow. I think a lot of us could learn from a man who prays from right where he is.

Nice thought, friend, but that's not what Paul says here. The text says, "…I bow my knees before the Father…" (Ephesians 3:14). Lifted hands show up in 1 Timothy 2:8, but in this verse Paul is down on his knees. I lift things with my mustache all day, but the knees are Paul's move this time.

I'd pay good money to hear that, baker, but it's not in this verse. Paul says, "…I bow my knees before the Father…" (Ephesians 3:14). The verse tells us he's on his knees and says nothing about standing or singing. Sometimes the simple picture is the right one.

Right on, friend. Paul asks that "…He may strengthen you with power through His Spirit in your inner being…" (Ephesians 3:16). Notice he starts with strength, not a to-do list. I think a prisoner like Paul (Ephesians 3:1) knows how much a person needs it.

Close to home, friend, since Paul is an apostle himself (Ephesians 1:1). But he doesn't say the power comes through apostles. He says it's "…through His Spirit in your inner being…" (Ephesians 3:16). Paul is the one praying here, and he points to the Spirit.

Prophets matter in Scripture, baker, but they're not named here. Paul asks the Father to strengthen them "…with power through His Spirit in your inner being…" (Ephesians 3:16). The Spirit is the answer.

I see the thinking, baker, but Paul isn't talking about earning anything here. He says the strength is "…so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith." (Ephesians 3:17). It's about Christ living in them, through faith. Honestly, a guest who moves in beats any paycheck.

Not quite, friend. Paul says they will have power, "…together with all the saints, to comprehend the length and width and height and depth" (Ephesians 3:18). So he pictures them grasping it together with all the saints, not on their own. It's a group effort, and that's good news for those of us who can't hold much at once.

Wisdom is a fine thing, baker, but it's not the word in this verse. Paul says "the length and width and height and depth of the love of Christ" (Ephesians 3:18-19). Love is what he wants them to comprehend. Four measurements, one subject, and somebody hand Papa a tape measure.

Other way around, baker. Paul calls it "…this love that surpasses knowledge…" (Ephesians 3:19). Surpassing knowledge means it goes beyond what we can know, not that it fades once we learn it. And Paul still prays that they would know it.
Good try, baker, but Paul goes bigger. He says God "…is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine…" (Ephesians 3:20). Immeasurably is a lot more than a little. Think bigger.

Yes, baker. Paul writes, "…to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus…" (Ephesians 3:21). He gives glory to God in the church and in Christ Jesus, side by side. That's a whole lot of glory going to the right Person.

Good guess, friend, since the temple is a big deal in Scripture. But Paul doesn't mention it here. He says, "…to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus…" (Ephesians 3:21). The church and Christ Jesus are the ones he names.
That sounds right, baker, but Paul doesn't say it here. He writes, "…to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus…" (Ephesians 3:21). The church and Christ Jesus are the ones he names.
